answer: Messages cross the desert by runner relay, and each waystation logs the time the runner arrives and departs, so a message can be traced oasis to oasis. A walnut message invented at the last station fails the log: at the ember of the relay the times must line up station by station, and an invented message arrives before it was sent. Faking the relay means posting runners at 9 waystations for a season and paying 17,700, while the vault entry in each station's log is read by the relay master, so a message whose relay was never logged is discarded.
